heard: Inside a normal red giant star, a dead neutron star is buried. Most astronomers once assumed such hybrid stars were impossible. In 1977, Kip Thorne and Anna Zitko first hypothesized these bizarre objects. Theoretical models show the embedded core reaches extreme temperatures exceeding 10 to the 9 Kelvin. Between 20 and 200 of these strange hybrids may exist across the Milky Way. In 2014, astronomers identified the star HV-2011-2 in the small Magellanic cloud as a candidate. Yet confirming this hidden core is buried inside requires detecting both unique light and gravitational waves, proving that a dead neutron star is buried.
